name: Ifrane Centre
tagline: The alpine grid with the Lion Stone
description: The core of the town the French laid out in the 1930s, pitched roofs and wide clean streets around the Lion Stone sculpture, with the cafes, the small shops and most of the hotels. It is walkable, orderly and completely unlike any other Moroccan town centre.
bestFor: Short stays and anyone without a car
pros: Everything walkable in a clean compact grid
Cedar forest starts at the edge of town
cons: Cold and snowy for months in winter

name: Al Akhawayn Quarter
tagline: The streets around the English-language university
description: The residential area beside Al Akhawayn University, whose American curriculum and English instruction give this corner of Morocco a distinctly international feel. Housing here is newer, English is widely spoken and the university's facilities dominate the local rhythm.
bestFor: Anyone connected to the university or wanting English spoken
pros: English spoken far more than anywhere nearby
cons: Empties entirely in the university holidays
The most expensive part of town
Life revolves around the academic calendar

name: Hay Riad
tagline: The ordinary Moroccan neighbourhood behind the postcard
description: The residential quarter where much of Ifrane's working population lives, plainer than the chalet streets and considerably cheaper. It has the everyday shops, the local cafes and the market, and it is where a long stay actually becomes affordable.
bestFor: Longer stays on a Moroccan rather than a visitor budget
pros: Ten minutes on foot to the centre
cons: Fewer cafes and no visitor services
Heating is a real issue in older stock

name: Michlifen and the Forest Road
tagline: Up towards the ski area and the cedars
description: The road southwest towards the Michlifen crater and the ski area, running through cedar forest where the Barbary macaques live. A few chalets and mountain hotels sit along it, and it is where anyone here for skiing or forest walking wants to be.
bestFor: Skiers in winter and forest walkers the rest of the year
pros: Cedar forest and the macaques at the door
Closest to the Michlifen ski area
cons: Snow can close the road in winter

name: Azrou
tagline: The larger Berber town down the road
description: A working town about seventeen kilometres southwest, considerably larger and more Moroccan than Ifrane, with a proper weekly souk, a cedar woodcarving trade and the road to the Middle Atlas plateau. Rents and food cost a fraction of what they do in Ifrane.
bestFor: Budget stays wanting a genuine Moroccan town nearby
pros: Much cheaper than Ifrane for everything
Weekly souk and a real local economy
Cedar forest and the macaque site nearby
cons: None of Ifrane's cleanliness or order
